1.title: Older than it should be
1.scope: The weathering of the Great Sphinx and the walls of its ditch (enclosure), and what it implies for the Sphinx's age. On the proponents' side: Robert Schoch's argument from precipitation-induced weathering (the rounded, deeply fissured profile of the enclosure walls, the coving), his seismic refraction work with Thomas Dobecki on the depth of subsurface weathering under the enclosure floor (front versus back), John Anthony West, and how Hancock and Bauval use it; Schoch's later updates (the date moving with time, his later books). On the reply's side: Mark Lehner and Zahi Hawass (the Khafre-era quarrying sequence, the Sphinx Temple's blocks), K. Lal Gauri's salt-crystallisation (haloclasty) mechanism, James Harrell's wet-sand hypothesis, Colin Reader's run-off argument (which supports an earlier-than-Khafre Sphinx, but only by a few centuries), David Coxill, and any newer work, including the yardang (wind-eroded landform) origin experiments of 2023 and any 2020s geological study of the enclosure. Include the climate record the argument depends on: when Giza last had enough rain to weather limestone this way (the Holocene humid phase and its end).

2.title: A lion, not a king
2.scope: The Sphinx as originally a lion, its human head a later re-carving, too small for the body; and the lion facing due east at the equinox sunrise when Leo rose with the sun, c. 10,500 BCE. On the proponents' side: Hancock and Bauval (The Message of the Sphinx / Keeper of Genesis, 1996), Schoch and West on the head, Robert Temple's Anubis variant (2009), the 1993 comparison of the face with Khafre's statue by the NYPD forensic artist Frank Domingo for West, the head's proportions measured against the body. On the reply's side: Lehner's photogrammetric survey of the Sphinx (the ARCE Sphinx Project) and his case for Khafre, the geology of the head (the harder bedrock member) as the reason for its size and preservation, the solstice and equinox alignments Lehner reads into the Sphinx Temple and the akhet of the two pyramids, and the history of the zodiac: when the Egyptians first pictured Leo as a lion (the Mesopotamian origin of the zodiac, the Ptolemaic Dendera zodiac). Give the precessional dates at stake: when the sun at the vernal equinox stood in Leo, by which constellation boundaries, and what Seked's sky package could compute to show it.

3.title: Temples of the same stone
3.scope: The Sphinx Temple and Khafre's Valley Temple: their limestone core blocks (some estimated at 100 tons or more) quarried from the Sphinx enclosure, the same strata as the Sphinx's body, and the claim that this core was already weathered when the granite casing was laid over it, the granite's back cut to fit the eroded limestone. On the proponents' side: Schoch, West, Hancock, and any measurement of the block sizes and of the casing's fit. On the reply's side: Herbert Ricke's study of the Sphinx Temple (1970), Uvo Hölscher's 1912 excavation of the Khafre temples (source id hoelscher-1912 is in data/sources.json), Mariette's 1860 discovery of the Khafre statues in the Valley Temple, Lehner's tying of the temples' blocks to the enclosure's quarrying layer by layer, the Khafre inscriptions on the granite, and any 2000s to 2020s work on these temples (the Giza Plateau Mapping Project, AERA). Also the Osireion at Abydos, which Hancock and others compare.

4.title: The First Time
4.scope: Zep Tepi (sp tpj, 'the First Time'), the Followers of Horus (Shemsu Hor), and the Egyptian king lists that put gods and spirits before the kings: the Turin Royal Canon and Manetho as transmitted by Eusebius and Syncellus, with the lengths of reign they give. The Inventory Stela (found by Mariette in 1858, Twenty-sixth Dynasty) and its statement that the Sphinx and a temple of Isis already stood in Khufu's time. The Edfu Building Texts (Reymond 1969) as Hancock and Bauval use them. The Pyramid Texts of Unas at Saqqara (c. 2350 BCE): the utterances in which the king becomes a star with Orion (Sah) and the stars of the north, with their utterance numbers, in Faulkner's and Allen's translations. On the reply's side: the Inventory Stela as late pious fiction, the mythic rather than dated character of Zep Tepi, the scholarly reading of the star religion (Faulkner 1966, Allen 2005, Krauss 1997), and the standard dates of Egyptian chronology (Hornung, Krauss and Warburton 2006; the radiocarbon chronology of Bronk Ramsey et al. 2010).

5.title: The sky as a clock
5.scope: The Orion correlation and the Great Pyramid's shafts. Bauval's correlation of the three Giza pyramids with Orion's belt (Discussions in Egyptology 13, 1989; The Orion Mystery with Gilbert, 1994: source id bauval-gilbert-1994): the size, offset and angle of the three, the Nile as the Milky Way, and the claim that the belt's angle to the meridian and its culmination altitude match the ground best at its precessional low point, c. 10,500 BCE. The shafts: Trimble and Badawy (1964) on the King's Chamber south shaft and Orion's belt, Bauval on the Queen's Chamber south shaft and Sirius, Gantenbrink's 1993 robot survey of the shaft angles (gantenbrink-1993), and the alignment dates c. 2450 BCE (Seked's own solver writes docs/shafts.md). On the reply's side: Krupp 1997 (krupp-1997) and Fairall 1999 (fairall-1999) on the correlation's orientation and its fit at 10,500 BCE, Legon, Belmonte, and any statistical test of the correlation (Orofino and others). Say exactly which numbers Seked can compute with packages/sky (Vondrák 2011 precession) to show the belt's altitude and angle across the slider's range from today to 10,500 BCE.

6.title: Numbers in the stone
6.scope: The mathematics read into the Great Pyramid: perimeter over height equal to 2π, apothem over half-base equal to φ (and the Herodotus face-area reading, Taylor 1859), the 1:43,200 scale of the Northern Hemisphere (Stecchini via Tompkins 1971: tompkins-1971; Hancock 1995: hancock-1995), the latitude near 30° N, and the orientation to true north within a few arcminutes (Cole 1925: cole-1925). On the reply's side: the seked of 5½ palms (the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus problems 56 to 60) from which both π and φ follow to within the survey's error, Roger Herz-Fischler's The Shape of the Great Pyramid (2000), Corinna Rossi 2004 (rossi-2004), the arbitrariness of 43,200, and the methods proposed for finding north: Spence 2000 (spence-2000) with the stars, Belmonte 2001, Magli, and Dash 2015 (dash-2015) with the equinox shadow. Read data/claims/ for the claims Seked already evaluates, and report their residuals as the receipts.

7.title: Before the flood
7.scope: The Younger Dryas (about 12,900 to 11,700 years before present) and Göbekli Tepe. The Younger Dryas impact hypothesis as its proponents make it (Firestone et al. 2007, the Comet Research Group, Moore et al. 2020 on Abu Hureyra, Sweatman and Tsikritsis on Pillar 43) and its critics (among them Holliday et al. 2023, and any retraction among the papers involved). Göbekli Tepe: Klaus Schmidt's excavations and dates (c. 9600 to 8200 BCE), the enclosures, the carved pillars, the claim that hunter-gatherers built monuments before farming, pottery or metal, and that the enclosures were deliberately buried. Then, as the reply must include it, the excavation reports since 2019 by the DAI team (Lee Clare, Moritz Kinzel, Oliver Dietrich, Jens Notroff and others): domestic buildings, cisterns and water channels, cereal processing, and the backfill possibly caused by slope slides as well as deliberate burial; and the Taş Tepeler sites (Karahan Tepe). Also the Society for American Archaeology's 2022 letter on Ancient Apocalypse, and what Hancock says in reply. Keep the two questions apart: what Göbekli Tepe shows about the age of monumental building, and whether it bears on Giza at all.

8.title: What would settle it
8.scope: The tests that could decide the Sphinx's age and what lies under it, and where each stands. Coring or drilling the Sphinx enclosure floor to measure the depth of weathering that Dobecki and Schoch inferred from seismic refraction (dobecki-schoch-1992). Physical dating of carved surfaces: surface luminescence dating of Egyptian monuments (Liritzis and others), cosmogenic nuclide exposure dating and its difficulty for limestone, and dating sediments in the enclosure. The radiocarbon dating of mortar from the pyramids (the 1984 and 1995 projects, Bonani et al. 2001) and what it says about construction. The cavities under and around the Sphinx: the 1990s seismic and ground-penetrating radar surveys, the 'Hall of Records' (cayce), what has and has not been surveyed since, and the 2025 radar claims about Khafre's pyramid (khafre-project-2025) and their reception. The muon surveys of the Great Pyramid (ScanPyramids: morishima-2017, procureur-2023) as the model of an instrumented answer. For each test: who has proposed it, what result would favour each side, and why it has or has not been done (permits, cost, the Supreme Council of Antiquities).
